summary: Draws every expedition GET /api/expeditions returns (the shop's three seeded expeditions plus the signed-in adventurer's own) as geodesic polylines on the existing Aurelis globe in ReagentMapView.vue, tagged with saturdayMetadata like the site entities already are, and makes each entry in the site list a control that flies the camera to that site, bringing it onto the near side of the globe even when it starts on the far side. Purely additive within the pattern reagent-map-globe already established (per-entity saturdayMetadata tagging, the window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ seam, the fetch-with-timeout API client shape) — no new package, endpoint, or layer boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The view MUST draw every expedition GET /api/expeditions returns for the current adventurer as a geodesic polyline, both ends within 1 km of its stored ends, tagged with saturdayMetadata { id, name, kind: 'expedition' }.
examples: Signed out: 'Spring to Crag', 'Glade to Caves', and 'Cairn to Shoals' are drawn (spec AC3).
Signed in as Elara: the three seeded expeditions plus 'Moonwell Spring to Frostcap Hollow' are drawn; 'Ember Crag to Saltmarsh Cairn' is not drawn (spec AC4).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Choosing a site from the list MUST fly the camera so that site lands on screen on the near side of the globe, including a site that starts on the far side.
examples: From the default view, Tidewrack Shoals is on the far side; choosing it from the list brings it on screen on the near side (spec AC5).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The @visual globe baseline MUST change only because the newly drawn expeditions now appear in it. Regenerate it in both runner images, view each changed PNG, and record what changed and why. No other baseline changes, and no tolerance is raised.
examples: Run scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh --update-baselines and --ubi9 --update-baselines; only globe-default-view.png differs in each image; reagent-map-header.png, reagent-site-list.png, and reagent-map-error.png stay byte-identical.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every new or changed function MUST keep cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail, and no file outside scope.paths MUST change except this order's own delivery record under docs/features/reagent-map-expeditions/.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The reagent map MUST send no request outside the app's own origin or the mock API's own origin, including the new expeditions fetch.

The expeditions client MAY attach an Authorization Bearer header from localStorage('dnd_auth_token'), mirroring orders.ts's pattern, but MUST NOT require one: GET /api/expeditions already tolerates an absent or invalid token.
Each site-list entry MUST stay operable by keyboard (Enter/Space activates it) and MUST expose an accessible name that announces it flies the camera to that site, once it becomes a clickable control.

developer: Create apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/src/api/expeditions.ts: types GeoPoint {lat,lng} and Expedition {id, name?, owner, from: GeoPoint, to: GeoPoint} matching lib/api/ShopApi.ts's shape; fetchExpeditions(): Promise<Expedition[]> against `${API_BASE}/api/expeditions`, same runtime API_BASE resolution and AbortController 5s timeout as reagentSites.ts.

In fetchExpeditions(), attach `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from localStorage('dnd_auth_token') only when a token is present, mirroring orders.ts's getAuthHeaders but omitting Content-Type (this is a GET).
In ReagentMapView.vue, import fetchExpeditions and add an `expeditions` ref alongside the existing `sites` ref.

Extend onMounted's Promise.allSettled to [buildViewer(), fetchReagentSites(), fetchExpeditions()]; if either the sites or the expeditions promise rejects, destroy the viewer and set mapError to the existing exact text 'Failed to load reagent sites. Try refreshing the page.' — do not reword it, since reagent-map-error.png's baseline must not change.

Add addExpeditionEntities(Cesium, viewer, ellipsoid, expeditions): for each expedition add a polyline entity from Cesium.Cartesian3.fromDegreesArray([from.lng, from.lat, to.lng, to.lat], ellipsoid) with arcType: Cesium.ArcType.GEODESIC, tagged saturdayMetadata { id, name: expedition.name ?? '', kind: 'expedition' }.
Call addExpeditionEntities after addSiteEntities in onMounted's happy path, once both sites and expeditions have resolved.

Wrap each site-list item's text in a `<button type="button">` that calls flyToSite(site) on click; reset its appearance (no border/background/margin change from the current plain text) so reagent-site-list.png's baseline does not change; give it an accessible name such as aria-label="Fly to {{ site.name }}" and a stable data-testid per site.

Add flyToSite(site: ReagentSite): keep the Cesium module and ellipsoid returned by buildViewer() in component-scope variables (same lifetime as `viewer`) and call viewer.camera.flyTo({ destination: Cesium.Cartesian3.fromDegrees(site.lng, site.lat, FLY_TO_HEIGHT_METERS, ellipsoid) }); do not special-case any one site.

Add a third failure-path case to reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts: fetchExpeditions() rejecting after buildViewer() and fetchReagentSites() both resolve still destroys the viewer and leaves no canvas, no __SATURDAY_CESIUM__, and no site-list items, across repeated mounts — same assertion shape as the two existing cases.

edgeCases.case: fetchExpeditions() rejects after buildViewer() and fetchReagentSites() both resolve
edgeCases.handling: Treat identically to a reagent-sites fetch failure: destroy the viewer and set mapError to the existing message, unchanged, so reagent-map-error.png's baseline does not change.

edgeCases.case: An expedition has no name (Expedition.name is optional per lib/api/ShopApi.ts)
edgeCases.handling: saturdayMetadata.name falls back to '' rather than undefined, so every consumer of cesium.getEntities() always receives a string.

edgeCases.case: A site is clicked again while a previous camera flight is still animating
edgeCases.handling: Cesium's camera.flyTo cancels the in-flight animation and starts the new one; no extra guard is added.

edgeCases.case: Choosing a site already on the near side of the globe
edgeCases.handling: flyToSite behaves the same for any site; AC5's far-side scenario (Tidewrack Shoals) is the one the test exercises, not a special case in the implementation.

edgeCases.case: A signed-in adventurer who is neither Elara nor Borin, with no expeditions of their own
edgeCases.handling: GET /api/expeditions returns only the three seeded expeditions, same as signed out; no client-side filtering is added — the server already enforces visibility.
